CITY OF SAN GABRIEL

  Tuesday, August 25, 2020 – 6:30 P.M.

  City Hall Council Chamber
  425 South Mission Drive
  San Gabriel, California 91776

Pursuant to State and County Directives, San Gabriel City Hall is closed to the public and physical access
to the meeting has been suspended. To provide members of the public access to the meeting and an
opportunity to comment on items on and off the Agenda, the following opportunities have been
established:

Public Comments

Please email all public comments on this agenda only to cityclerk@sgch.org and include the following on
the subject line of your email: PUBLIC COMMENT: 08/25/20 Special Meeting. The Clerk will read public
comments into the record for up to the three-minute limit. Words that would disrupt the meeting,
including profanity, obscenity, and discriminatory language, will not be read.

Watch the Meeting Online

Live broadcasts of the meetings are available using the following link:
City Council Meeting Videos
Spectrum cable: Live streaming on Channel 3, Public Access Channel.

  Tuesday, August 25, 2020

   CALL TO ORDER
   ROLL CALL: Mayor Menchaca, Vice Mayor Liao, Council Members Ding,
  Harrington, Pu

 1. PUBLIC COMMENT

 2. CONTINUED ITEM

  A. MISSION PLAYHOUSE DISCUSSION – UPDATED AUGUST 21, 2020

  Each year, the City subsidizes the Mission Playhouse operations by an average
  of $735,000. As this amount has become unsustainable for the General Fund
  in this economic situation, Staff is presenting options for the future operation
  of the Mission Playhouse. Due to an overwhelming amount of over 300 public
  comments received for this item, the City Council voted to move the item to
  a Special Council Meeting on August 25. The public comments received prior
  to August 20, the day prior to posting of this revised report, have been
  entered into the record and are included as Attachment A to this updated
  staff report.

  Select the links below to access the staff report and attachments.
  Staff Report
  Attachment A
  Attachment B
  Attachment C
  Attachment D

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council discuss this item and provide direction
  to Staff.

 3. ADJOURNMENT

  The next regular City Council meeting will be held on Tuesday, September 1, 2020
  at 6:30 p.m. Information regarding matters to be considered at each meeting will
  be available on the Friday before the City Council Meeting on the City’s website
  at www.sangabrielcity.com.

Questions about this Agenda? Should any person have a question concerning any of

Any person with a disability who requires a modification or accommodation in order to
participate in a meeting should direct such a request to the City Clerk Department by
emailing cityclerk@sgch.org at least 48 hours before the meeting, if possible.

MINUTES OF AUGUST 25, 2020
  SPECIAL MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCIL

CALL TO ORDER

Mayor Menchaca called the special meeting of the San Gabriel City Council to order at
6:31 p.m. on Tuesday, August 25, 2020, with all Council Members and staff participating
by teleconference.

ROLL CALL

Council Members Present:  Tony Ding, John R. Harrington, Jason Pu, Vice Mayor
  Chin Ho Liao, and Mayor Denise Menchaca.
Council Members Absent:  None.
Staff Members Present:  City Manager Mark Lazzaretto, City Attorney Keith
  Lemieux,  Assistant  City  Manager/Community
  Development Director Arminé Chaparyan, Community
  Services/Interim Mission Playhouse Director Rebecca
  Perez, Police Chief Eugene Harris, Chief City Clerk
  Sharon Clark, Public Works Director/City Engineer Greg
  de Vinck, Fire Chief Steven Wallace, Human
  Resources/Risk Management Director Edward Macias,
  Interim Finance Director Kenneth Louie, and Assistant
  City Clerk Marilyn Bonus.

1. PUBLIC COMMENT

  Chasity Jennings-Nuñez provided comments expressing concerns about racial equity
  and commending the City’s creation of the Human Equity, Access and Relations (HEAR)
  Commission.

  G. Sanchez provided comments stating that if a government entity would like to tax
  wages earned by undocumented individuals, they should be counted in full.

2. NEW BUSINESS

  A. MISSION PLAYHOUSE DISCUSSION – UPDATED AUGUST 21, 2020

  The staff presentation was made by Community Services/Interim Mission
  Playhouse Director Rebecca Perez.

  Chief City Clerk Clark announced that comments that were received for the item
  when originally scheduled last week had been included in the staff report
  attachments for this meeting, which had been made available to the City Council
  and the public since the meeting was posted on August 21, 2020, and comments
  to be read tonight were received since then.

  In general support of the Mission Playhouse: Annemarie Werthwein; Terry L.
  Babcock; Leilani Wilmore; Diane Lam; TCHS Student; Gina Baffo, Arts Consultant,
  Outreach, Pasadena Civic Ballet; and an anonymous commenter.

  Chasity Jennings-Nuñez provided comments requesting the involvement of the
  Historic Preservation Commission before any decisions are made.

  Donn Linton provided comments requesting consideration of the maintenance
  needs of the Wurlitzer pipe organ in the Mission Playhouse.

  Discussion included solicitation of donors and fundraising suggestions, including
  GoFundMe; demand for theater venues; charging lower rates and expanding
  available days of use; diversity of performances; delay on restorative exterior
  painting due to the need to redesign the project pursuant to the recent nomination
  of the Playhouse to the National Register of Historic Places; status of grant funding
  for exterior painting; performing maintenance while the Playhouse is closed due to
  COVID-19 restrictions; Facility Fee fund balance and yearly revenue, including
  parking fees; long-term strategic planning; facilitating filming productions; detail
  on budget line items; staffing levels; clarification that under an emergency
  Executive Order the public comments submitted for the last meeting do not have
CITY COUNCIL SPECIAL MEETING MINUTES  Page 4 of 5  August 25, 2020
   to be read aloud as they were included in the staff report for the item tonight;
  revenue to date; marketing outreach pursuant to COVID-19 guidelines; forming a
  501(c)(3) to accept donations; referral networks; post-COVID planning; cost-
  savings for other staff management models; mindset of subsidizing versus funding;
  value provided by the Playhouse to the City; pricing changes already in place;
  beneficial impact of Playhouse events on surrounding businesses; inclusion of
  relevant commission input; implementing a plan for the Playhouse during COVID-
  19 restrictions similar to the 10-Point Plan for Recovery, Resiliency, and
  Reinvestment, that could include organizational-structure, arts-development
  impact fees, reviewing existing contracts for fee appropriateness, fundraising,
  partnerships with local businesses for recognition, subscription options, grant
  opportunities, establishment of a 501(c)(3), expanding marketing and
  communication capacity, forming relationships with local news organizations,
  maintaining relationships with rental clients, filming opportunities, branding,
  virtual performances, advertising outside of the state and country, revenue-
  generating activities during COVID, and parking lot repair; and a possible future
  advisory committee.

  There was a consensus of the City Council to direct staff to pursue Scenario/Option
  3 as listed in the staff report under which the Playhouse will remain open in a
  limited capacity through December 2020, allowing for livestreaming and filming
  events to continue; provide detailed line item information to Council in the future;
  and to move forward with full re-opening of the Playhouse once health orders
  allow.

  City Manager Lazzaretto recognized Mission Playhouse Manager Elias Bourjeli for
  a great job managing the Playhouse, and expressed his gratitude to Community
  Services/Interim Mission Playhouse Director Perez for a job well-done directing
  two departments.

  Mayor Menchaca gave a special thanks to Chief City Clerk Clark and her team for
  a good job responding to the many public comments for this item and for
  representing the City well; and to Mission Playhouse Manager Bourjeli and
  Community Services/Interim Mission Playhouse Director Perez for their patience,
  work, and great information.

3. ADJOURNMENT
